We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge 1.56).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/c59a56406bcd9bd54e34c2bbeffca20ae0633d654a4c69f32aca3569e9ad2f20.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 1.56) & =1-P(Z<1.56) \\  & =1-Φ(1.56)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/eb5bf827193cff372f78486d5e2ca26c63a6e310f415ffcc0b91539e79c7a566.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(1.56)=0.9406.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge 1.56) & =1-Φ(1.56) \\  & =1-0.9406 \\  & =0.0594.\end{aligned}
$$
